observations.statement: RM-045 permits an attached UI session to surface a dashboard badge or notification, forbids GUI-only recovery such as Open in Terminal in headless contexts, and requires alternative recovery guidance categories.

RM-046 assigns mutation_capable declaration to the tool registry as a boolean defaulting false, propagation to the node planner, and attempt/safe-point gating to run modes without allowing modes to redefine the classifier.

RM-047 requires identity, account selection, pressure ownership, blocked-sequence persistence, startup recovery, DAE policy ownership, and usage-role continuity across mode changes and blocked recovery.

RM-001 is retired migration-lineage compatibility metadata; fine-grained PlanUnits own implementation-facing coverage, and the bridge may neither override them nor use source_preserving_planunit compile mode.

The migration section names four run-scoped proof artifacts, records the three atomization/disposition batches, and states that the batches changed neither generated governance artifacts nor implementation/runtime task artifacts.

RM-048 states that containerized-host availability does not widen authority, HTE is the default for Puppet Master hosted dispatch, DAE requires existing run-mode and provider policy, and yolo remains DAE with mandatory guardrails.
RM-048 denies mutation and several host-side actions based solely on discovery/configuration/GUI availability and enumerates eight blocked host outcome tokens that remain blocked rather than failed.

RM-048 acceptance requires existing DAE guardrails, FileSafe scans, permission snapshots, and receipt chains for DAE/yolo host work, and requires blocked outcomes to be counted and surfaced as blocked states.
The FABLE addendum treats unresolved P5 recovery requirements as owner-routed governance blockers rather than live mode behavior and names six blocker record fields.
The FABLE addendum states that YOLO skips only optional prompts and that FileSafe, permissions, policy, secret, protected-branch, and remote-side-effect guards still block or require approval.

RM-049 requires UsageRecord settlement and background-contribution identity to survive six run-mode surfaces and many partial, retry, blocked, provider-failure, and adjustment outcomes while preserving named identity, settlement, and rollup fields.
RM-049 directs GUI consumers to render six states distinctly and forbids treating blocked runtime outcomes as either zero usage or final settled cost.

RM-049 acceptance covers non-final partial/aborted streams, once-only accepted retry/escalation usage with retained failed or superseded attempts, blocked-state rendering, and attributable hidden/background contribution references.
Both new addenda expressly avoid creating runtime dispatch or executable build artifacts; their node compile hints also disable WorkNode and NodeSeed creation.
RM-048 and RM-049 identify plan validation now but describe their behavioral fixture suites as future validation surfaces.
Context only: the immediately preceding RM-044 defines blocked_notice, headless_ask_denied, unavailable/headless status, and operation-card consumers when no interactive presenter exists.

candidate_findings.title: Headless recovery guidance lacks a consumable contract
candidate_findings.statement: RM-045 requires six categories of alternative guidance but does not define a payload schema, delivery channel, required content, cause-to-option mapping, ordering, or what must happen when an option is unavailable.
candidate_findings.impact: CLI, orchestrator, notification, and operation-card implementations can expose incompatible or non-actionable recovery paths for the same blocked state.

candidate_findings.title: Attached-session blocked discoverability is discretionary
candidate_findings.statement: RM-045 says an attached UI session may surface a badge or notification, so the core does not require any UI-visible blocked signal or define its trigger, update, clearing, persistence, or accessibility behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: A blocked headless run can remain invisible or stale in an attached UI, and builders can implement materially different discovery behavior.

candidate_findings.title: RM-045 through RM-047 lack behavioral acceptance oracles
candidate_findings.statement: The accepted requirements use lineage/addressability acceptance language and only migration/index validation surfaces; the core supplies no fixtures or executable checks for the GUI exclusion, mutation gating, or runtime-identity continuity behaviors.
candidate_findings.impact: Structural validators can pass while safety-sensitive and recovery-sensitive runtime behavior remains absent or incorrect.

candidate_findings.title: Mutation gating and safe-point decisions have no deterministic mode contract
candidate_findings.statement: RM-046 says modes control whether mutation-capable attempts may occur and whether safe points are relevant, but the core defines no per-mode allow/deny matrix, enforcement point, denied-attempt status, transition behavior, or safe-point decision rule; regular/yolo and ask/plan appear only as preserved tokens in this PlanUnit.
candidate_findings.impact: Planner and executor implementations can disagree, allow mutation in a prohibited mode, or omit a required safe point.

candidate_findings.title: Runtime identity continuity is named but not operationalized
candidate_findings.statement: RM-047 lists identity and recovery obligations but gives no field types or nullability, atomic handoff boundary, blocked_sequence uniqueness/idempotency rule, startup-handshake state machine, persistence failure behavior, or conflict resolution across account switch and mode change.
candidate_findings.impact: Recovery can misattribute usage or authority, duplicate blocked events, lose policy state, or resume under the wrong operational identity.

candidate_findings.title: Host authority selection has no resolver precedence or failure contract
candidate_findings.statement: RM-048 establishes HTE defaulting and conditional DAE/yolo authority but does not identify the selecting authority or persisted selection, define precedence among run mode, provider policy, host policy, and guardrails, or specify the result when those inputs conflict or become unavailable.
candidate_findings.impact: Equivalent host actions can receive different privilege decisions, and an unsafe resolver can interpret availability or an explicit selection as effective authority.

candidate_findings.title: Blocked host outcome taxonomy lacks mapping and lifecycle semantics
candidate_findings.statement: RM-048 enumerates blocked codes and requires blocked-not-failed accounting, but it does not map conditions to codes, define precedence for simultaneous blockers, specify required payload/evidence, or define retry, cancellation, recovery, and terminal transitions.
candidate_findings.impact: Producers can emit incompatible reason codes and consumers can miscount, retry indefinitely, or settle a still-blocked host action incorrectly.

candidate_findings.title: Accepted host safety behavior has no current executable oracle
candidate_findings.statement: RM-048 is accepted, yet its host-authority and blocked-outcome behavioral checks are explicitly future fixtures; the only current validation surface named here is plan-index validation.
candidate_findings.impact: Mandatory guardrails, authority boundaries, and blocked accounting cannot be certified from the specified current validation surface.

candidate_findings.title: Owner-routed blocker records lack schema and transition semantics
candidate_findings.statement: The FABLE repair names blocker fields but does not define their types, required/null rules, identifier uniqueness, allowed status values, owner reference validation, state transitions, or how and when reopen_condition is evaluated.
candidate_findings.impact: Governance tools can disagree about whether a blocker is open, resolved, or eligible to reopen, weakening owner-routed recovery tracking.

candidate_findings.title: YOLO guard classification and block-versus-approval choice are undefined
candidate_findings.statement: The safety rule distinguishes optional prompts from non-bypassable guards and says listed guards still block or require approval, but it does not define the classifier/authority, precedence among guards, when the outcome is block versus approval, or required denial/approval evidence.
candidate_findings.impact: A builder can classify a safety prompt as optional or choose approval where an unconditional block was intended, enabling protected or remote side effects.

candidate_findings.title: RM-049 is classified non-GUI despite normative GUI behavior
candidate_findings.statement: RM-049 sets gui_related false while its canonical text commands GUI consumers to render six states distinctly and its implementation surfaces include a runtime artifacts panel.
candidate_findings.impact: GUI-specific indexing, review, ownership, and build planning can omit a user-visible correctness requirement.

candidate_findings.title: Usage settlement and deduplication state machine is incomplete
candidate_findings.statement: RM-049 names preserved fields and requires once-only accepted usage through dedupe_key, but it does not define dedupe-key scope or derivation, settlement-status transitions, accepted/ignored precedence, ordering for retries, escalations, late events, and adjustments, or idempotent replay behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: The same provider work can be double-counted, dropped, or finalized differently across consumers, producing incorrect usage and cost.

candidate_findings.title: Background contribution rollup is ambiguously coupled to drill-through
candidate_findings.statement: RM-049 says hidden/background references are not folded into parent totals without drill-through but does not specify whether viewing drill-through changes aggregation, when contributions enter totals, or how accepted/ignored rollup state controls the parent.
candidate_findings.impact: Displayed and persisted totals can depend on UI interaction or differ between summary and detail consumers.

candidate_findings.title: GUI settlement statuses lack mapping and accessible distinction requirements
candidate_findings.statement: RM-049 lists streaming_partial, failed, adjusted, blocked, unknown, and settled as distinct render states but does not map overlapping runtime/provider conditions to one state, define transition and stale-state clearing rules, or require a non-color/accessibility-safe distinction.
candidate_findings.impact: GUI consumers can present conflicting status, misleading finality, or inaccessible distinctions for usage and cost.

candidate_findings.title: Usage settlement behavior has no current fixture oracle
candidate_findings.statement: RM-049 names plan-index and plan-gate validation but leaves the run-mode Usage settlement fixture suite for the future, despite acceptance obligations for partial streams, retries, blockers, and hidden contributions.
candidate_findings.impact: Governance can report success without executable evidence that billing-sensitive lifecycle and projection behavior works.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: RM-045 explicitly forbids Open in Terminal as a headless recovery affordance and enumerates the alternative guidance categories that must be provided.
RM-046 explicitly gives mutation_capable a safe default of false and prevents run modes from overriding the registry classification.
RM-001 explicitly states its retired authority boundary, fine-grained coverage replacement, and non-source-preserving compile mode.
RM-048 explicitly states that discovery/configuration/GUI availability is not mutation authority and cannot by itself authorize listed host-side effects or completion certification.
RM-048 explicitly preserves blocked != failed and requires blocked outcomes to be counted and surfaced as blocked rather than execution failures.
The FABLE addendum explicitly prevents YOLO from bypassing FileSafe, permission, policy, secret, protected-branch, and remote-side-effect guards.
RM-049 explicitly retains failed or superseded attempts during retry, forbids blocked outcomes from appearing as zero/final settled usage, and forbids fabricating missing provider usage.
The addenda explicitly avoid claiming executable runtime/build artifacts, and both PlanUnit compile hints disable WorkNode and NodeSeed creation.
The migration section explicitly enumerates proof artifact paths and batch-level span dispositions rather than leaving the retired bridge coverage implicit.

unknowns.statement: The assigned core does not establish whether RM-003, RM-008, and RM-009 fully define the HTE/DAE and ask/plan/regular/yolo resolver semantics referenced by RM-048.
The assigned core does not establish whether the external contract references define the exact per-mode mutation matrix, safe-point trigger, and denied-attempt behavior omitted from RM-046.
The assigned core does not establish whether the owner-hinted storage, permissions, provider, and usage documents define schemas and transactional recovery for RM-047 identity fields.
The HTE and DAE expansions and their complete behavioral boundaries are not defined inside the assigned core.
The listed future RM-048 and RM-049 fixture suites cannot be confirmed as implemented or scheduled from this window.
The assigned core does not establish whether an external governance schema defines the blocker status vocabulary and reopen_condition evaluation named by the FABLE repair.
The assigned core does not establish whether GUI owner documents resolve RM-049 status mapping, drill-through rollup, or accessibility behavior despite being named as implementation surfaces.
The migration proof artifacts are listed but were outside the permitted review inputs, so this result cannot establish whether they actually prove the stated coverage and dispositions.
The assigned core does not explain whether gui_related false on RM-049 is an intentional classification exception or a metadata defect.
The assigned core does not define the condition-to-display mapping for unknown versus failed, blocked, adjusted, streaming_partial, or settled usage states.

This addendum compiles containerized-host run-mode authority and blocked-outcome rules. It does not create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, runtime dispatch, implementation files, generated governance artifacts, or production build tasks.

Containerized-host availability does not widen run-mode authority. HTE remains the default posture when Puppet Master
  dispatches hosted actions, DAE is allowed only under existing run-mode and provider policy, and yolo remains DAE with
  mandatory guardrails. Apps/services under test, PM work, provider tools, agent harnesses, shells, and integration
  commands may use host capability context only where runtime execution is later enabled and authority allows it.
  Discovery/configuration/GUI availability is not permission to mutate, attach, expose ports, push images, inject
  secrets, use remote hosts, or certify completion. Blocked host outcomes such as permission_denied, filesafe_blocked,
  runtime_disabled, runtime_unavailable, capability_unavailable, host_untrusted, host_unreachable, and test_gap_policy
  remain `blocked != failed`.

This addendum repairs non-runtime run-mode rows without creating WorkNodes, implementation files, runtime artifacts, or PNC-019 evidence.

- Repairs `sfk-f6bc657026c94cc22b43a8b1`: unresolved P5 run-mode governance recovery requirements are tracked as owner-routed blockers, not live mode behavior. Fields are `blocker_id`, `owner_doc_ref`, `conflict_summary`, `status`, `reopen_condition`, and `created_at_utc`.

- Repairs `sfk-bc255c3a3c2b772302812837`: YOLO is never approval-free for non-bypassable guards. It skips only optional prompts; FileSafe, permissions, policy, secret, protected-branch, and remote-side-effect guards still block or require approval.

This addendum binds run-mode outcomes to UsageRecord settlement projection. It creates no WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, implementation files, runtime artifacts, generated wiring rows, production build tasks, final manifests, or PNC-019 receipts.

Run-mode outcomes preserve UsageRecord settlement lifecycle and hidden/background contribution identity across ask, plan, regular, yolo, HTE, and DAE surfaces. Partial streams, aborted streams, retries, escalations, blocked outcomes, permission denials, FileSafe blocks, runtime_disabled, provider failures, and adjusted settlements keep their usage_event_ref, provider_attempt_ref, attempt_id, dedupe_key, parent_usage_record_id, settlement_status, partial_reason, failure_class, and accepted/ignored rollup state.
GUI consumers render streaming_partial, failed, adjusted, blocked, unknown, and settled distinctly and do not treat blocked != failed runtime outcomes as zero usage or final settled cost.

  - Hidden/background contribution refs remain attributable across run modes and are not folded into parent totals without drill-through.
